proposed_explanatory_paragraph_plain_not: No orientation of M or of the screen is required. Indeed, in two orthonormal screen frames related by any O in O(2), including det O=-1, the optical matrices are related by B-hat=O^{-1}BO and sigma-hat=O^{-1}sigma O. Hence tr B and tr(sigma^2)=|sigma|^2 are invariant; all screen inner products and the rank of the Jacobi map are likewise invariant. The local normal-pair construction in lem-gr-fx-null-normal-plane-and-screen uses only the supplied time orientation and permits interchange of the two future null rays. No volume form, orientation-compatible frame, or global null normal pair is used. Supplying an orientation recovers the same constructions on the oriented subclass.
orientation_free_derivation: Local normal pairs: project the supplied future timelike N orthogonally off TS using the inverse positive Gram matrix, normalize the resulting timelike normal, and choose only a local unit spacelike complement. The two future rays are nu+e and nu-e. A sign change e to -e swaps them; no orientation or global labeling is used. The existing normal-plane lemma proves this under time orientation alone.

Positive screen: for any nonzero null ell, choose locally a smooth v with g(ell,v)=-1 and set n=v+(g(v,v)/2)ell. Then g(n,n)=0 and g(ell,n)=-1. The span of ell,n has inertia(1,1), its orthogonal complement is positive2-dimensional, and ell-perp=Rell direct-sum that complement. This realizes the smooth quotient without orienting either it or M. Native29 separately repairs the prior mistaken null-hypersurface normal-plane wording; do not overwrite its repair.

Expansion and shear: chi(X,Y)=g(nabla_X ell,Y) is extension-independent. Torsion-freeness gives chi(X,Y)-chi(Y,X)=-g(ell,[X,Y])=0. Positive normal rescaling gives chi(a ell)=a chi(ell) because g(ell,Y)=0. Thus q-inverse chi has intrinsic trace and trace-free part independent of an orientation. For local ray interchange the pair of expansion signs is permuted, which leaves trapping unchanged.

Frame independence: in an orthonormal screen frame change O in O(2), including det O=-1, endomorphism matrices transform by O-inverse B O. Therefore trace B, trace(sigma squared), and trace(curvature screen map) are unchanged; tr(sigma squared) equals the nonnegative sum of squared entries since sigma is self-adjoint. Bilinear q contractions in the index form and its chi boundary term are likewise unchanged. No epsilon tensor is used.

Jacobi and Raychaudhuri: choose a parallel orthonormal screen frame along the parameter interval by metric-compatible parallel transport; this requires no orientation of a bundle over M. A-double-prime+Rscreen A=0 implies B-prime=-Rscreen-B squared, then theta-prime=-theta squared/2-|sigma| squared-Ric(ell,ell) by the null-basis contraction already proved. Every operation is tensorial or trace. Integrating (1/theta)-prime>=1/2 under negative theta and nonnegative Ric gives the existing focal bound. Rank loss of A is invariant under arbitrary invertible source/target basis changes; no signed determinant is needed.

Focal exclusion: index integrals use q inner products and ordinary affine-parameter integration on an interval, not an oriented surface integral. The negative-index field construction, endpoint-fixed exponential variations, future-cone selection via N, longitudinal null companion and causal push-up are unchanged by a screen reflection. Thus the orientation mismatch is removed without changing the independent native29 focal-extension/ODE repair obligations.

Global trapped-boundary chain: normalize each local future branch by g(ell,N)=-1, take the finite minimum of both negative expansions over a finite patch cover, apply focusing/exclusion, and take the finite union of compact normal-geodesic images. No global normal frame or surface orientation occurs. Penrose then uses achronality, flow projection and invariance of domain for topological three-manifolds; these do not assume orientation. Its volume-time supplier uses a volume density, not a globally chosen differential4-form.
